text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski died of a heart attack yesterday at the age of 41.

- Poland's parliament will probably deprive the former Main Customs Office head Ireneusz Sekula of parliamentary immunity. Sekula has been accused of paying too much to the listed Universal company for a contract it carried out for the office.
- Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR), the Polish Development Bank, has privately placed $50 million of Eurobonds.

- A direct Wroclaw-London air link is likely to start before the World Eucharistic Conference next year in the southwest Poland city, Wroclaw governor Janusz Zaleski said. British Midland is among six carriers interested in the route.
- Poland's major refinery, Petrochemia Plock (PP), will invest $1.9 billion in modernisation by the end of 1999.
- The economic climate in Poland's processing industry was worse in October than in the same period in 1995 and 1994, mainly due to a decline in exports, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Greenpeace has accused Poland and other central and eastern European countries of genetic experiments in agriculture and animal breeding conducted in open environment conditions.

- Poland's major insurance firm, Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen,(PZU SA), will increase its owned capital by up to $300 million in the first quarter of 1997, the company's new president Jan Monkiewicz said.

- The listed Mostostal Zabrze construction firm's new 2.6 million share issue will be sold at from 9.5 to 12 zlotys a share. The firm will soon present a list of the issue's guarantors, its president Leszek Pietrzak said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Polish financial institutions are most likely to become the main stakeholders in the PZU SA insurance firm following its privatisation, the PZU president said.
- Over 80 percent of production of Krakow-based Zaklady Przemyslu Tytonioowego (ZPTK) tobacco firm is from tobacco grown in Poland, ZPTK spokesperson Iwona Jaworska said.

- The state-owned CPN petrol distribution chain will start selling diesel oil coming from duty free import quotas. The imported oil price will not exceed 1.31 zlotys a litre, Polish Liquid Fuels Chamber president Andrzej Szczesniak said.

- The new Philips-made street lighting system in the Ketrzyn, northeastern Poland, will cut electricity bills by 40 percent and maintenance costs by 25 percent, the city's mayor Krzysztof Hecman said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Polish-made radar system TRD 1211 is capable of detecting F-117 stealth fighter aircraft, the Przemyslowy Instytut Telekomunikacji (PIT) industrial telecommunications institute president Roman Dufrene said.
- The German Lufthansa airlines will keep 80 weekly flights on Polish-German routes through the winter season, Lufthansa said.
- The 4WD Tractors firm, controlled by Same Deutz-Fahr Group, will invest five million German marks in a tractor plant it will open in Minkowice, Lublin province, 4WD president Marco Plebani said.
- The U.S. based Nibco PVC pipe maker has invested $3 million in the newly opened PCV and CPVC pipe factory in Lodz, central Poland.
ZYCIE
- The Polish market offers unlimited opportunities for Ford, Ford Distribution representative Nick Palmer said. The U.S. motor company's sales grew by 300 percent compared with last year's results.
- South Korea's KIA automaker, which entered Poland last year, sold 1500 cars to date and have recently introduced two new models KIA pride and KIA Clarus on the Polish market.
PARKIET
- CS First Boston brokerage house recommended buying the listed Exbud construction firm shares in a report dated October 23.
- The listed Paged wood processing firm has increased to 20 percent its stake in the Furnel International furniture maker.
